serviceTimeMs.how: mean = the Flask service (gunicorn)'s CPU per request at 1150 req/s net of idle: (32609 - 62 ms at rest) / 34500 requests = 0.9434 ms; shape (p95/median 0.7641/0.2500 ms) from the handler's own time; x 0.9638, the machine's thread speed at the pass (2.30 busy threads: the containers 1.02, k6 0.38, at rest 0.90)

clientLinkLatencyMs.how: anchored: (measured median 1.103 ms - the model's median without it 1.419 ms at 1150 req/s) / 2, one way, at least 0

serviceTimeByLoad.how: the staircase's work per request, its CPU per request net of idle times the machine's thread speed during the pass (1.5948 ms at 50, 1.2248 ms at 830, 1.2460 ms at 1150 req/s), fitted as a law of the rate, 1.216 + 18.94 × rate^-1 ms, over the top rate's (1.2321 ms); carried to 1,630 req/s, where the service's 2 CPUs fill, then flat

gcPauseMs.how: not modelled as a pause: each gunicorn worker collects on its own and stalls only its own request; the collections' CPU is in the CPU per request

writeServiceTimeMs.how: PostgreSQL's CPU per UPDATE with synchronous_commit off (0.1951 ms), shaped like its round trip (median 0.382, p95 1.721 ms)

readServiceTimeMs.how: PostgreSQL's CPU per SELECT (0.1527 ms, the pass's less its UPDATEs'), shaped like its round trip (median 0.361, p95 1.467 ms)

dbLinkLatencyMs.how: each way: the round trip the service measured less PostgreSQL's time, in two legs that keep its mean and variance (median 0.0828, p95 0.6590 ms)

dbCpuShare.how: PostgreSQL CPU per query at the top pass net of idle (0.1569 ms) / the model's mean time per query (31061 reads at 0.153 ms and 3439 writes without their flush at 0.195 ms: 0.157 ms); x 0.9638, the machine's thread speed at the pass (2.30 busy threads: the containers 1.02, k6 0.38, at rest 0.90)

commitFlushMs.how: PostgreSQL's own WAL flushes at 1150 req/s (pg_stat_wal): 3560 flushes of 1.058 ms on average, 0.97 commits per flush (the model: 1.00); shaped like the commit wait the service measured (p95/median 1.01, mean 1.217 ms)

serviceMemoryBaselineMb.how: at idle: the api-python-cores container's working set (the highest reading in each pass) against req/s over 10 points (at rest and 9 passes, 50 to 1,150 req/s), by non-negative least squares: 314.7 MiB + 0.0081 MiB per req/s, largest error at and above the median rate 4%

serviceMemoryPerRpsMb.how: per req/s: the api-python-cores container's working set (the highest reading in each pass) against req/s over 10 points (at rest and 9 passes, 50 to 1,150 req/s), by non-negative least squares: 314.7 MiB + 0.0081 MiB per req/s, largest error at and above the median rate 4%

serviceMemoryPerRequestMb.how: per request held: the floor, since the fit against req/s explains the whole working set (held requests' memory would count twice otherwise)
